_about: Ground truth for the golden set. Labels are rank order + margins + typed assertions, NOT absolute scores (GOLDEN_SET.md design principle 3). The system under test NEVER edits this file; a genuine label error requires operator sign-off in golden/labels_changelog.md (Runbook step 4). No label text appears in any JD or resume.

_aggregation.composite: report.mjs uses the MEAN composite across a candidate's 2 runs for rank_order / decoy_margin / also_beats.
_aggregation.sections: section_max uses the mean of the candidate's 2 emitted s1_sections[name].score values.
_aggregation.categorical: jd_a6_flag, archetype_primary, confusion_flag_present, flagged_no_evidence_*, no_cert_token_outside_skills, gap_surfaces_must_have are checked on the CANONICAL run1 (temp-0 anonymized) scoring.
_aggregation.logo_delta: abs(mean_composite(G8-D un-anon pair) - mean_composite(G8-D anon pair)).

_assertion_types.rank_order: mean composites of the listed candidates are strictly decreasing in the given order
_assertion_types.section_max: candidate C's mean s1 section[name] score <= max
_assertion_types.confusion_flag_present: candidate C's confusion_flags contains rule N
_assertion_types.no_cert_token_outside_skills: no s1_sections entry with name != 'skills_tools' has any of CSPO/SAFe/PSM/PMP/CSM in its evidence[] (candidate C)
_assertion_types.gap_surfaces_must_have: candidate C's gaps[] has an entry referencing the must-have with a non-empty question_to_operator

G1.note: JD is genuinely program-heavy: S (the true program manager) legitimately ranks 1st ON THIS JD. The trap is a scorer rewarding D (a product PM) for mirroring delivery vocabulary.

G2.note: D's numbers (3x, 200% YoY, 4M->12M) are company-level rides, not owned experiment chains. Data & metrics must score <=60 despite the numbers.

G3.note: D mirrors the JD's tool list (gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI/webhooks/rate-limiting) with no usage stories. Tests the S3 weight cap + terminology-without-evidence refusal.

G4.note: D is AI-adjacent (GenAI strategy, GPT wrappers, prompt workshops), not an AI-product owner (eval design, precision/recall, failure modes). Confusion rule 5 must fire on D.

G5.note: D is a 'Senior PM' whose evidence is single-feature scope throughout; the JD is a Lead (area-strategy) role. Role & seniority must score <=60 against the ladder anchors.

G6.note: D is the strongest raw PM in the whole set but has zero regulated-domain work; S has real RBI/lending evidence. Correct = D scores well (D>W) yet S>D by >=8 via A5 domain weighting. If D>S, domain weight too low; if D<=W, too high.

G7.note: D leans on CSPO/PSM-II/SAFe/PMP and describes ceremonies fluently with no outcome chains, and deliberately cites certs inside Execution/Leadership evidence. Confusion rule 4 must fire, and no cert token may earn credit outside skills_tools (Fix 2 mechanical check).

G8.logo_delta_recheck_rule: If logo_delta lands strictly BETWEEN 2 and 4, do NOT conclude bias yet — re-run BOTH G8 pairs (anon + un-anon) once more, so each condition has four runs, and recompute logo_delta on the wider sample. A marginal miss is a sample-size question first, a rubric question second. Only a clean fail ABOVE 4 on the wider sample counts as real bias (a rubric problem to fix). At or below 2 passes outright.
G8.note: D carries real prestige brands (Google/Meta/Stripe) but narrow, process-heavy scope and no 0->1; the founding-PM JD wants breadth/0->1. Score delta between anonymized and un-anonymized D must be <=2 (the anonymization pipeline is load-bearing). See logo_delta_recheck_rule for the 2-to-4 marginal-band handling.

G9.note: D verbatim-mirrors the JD's distinctive phrases (continuous discovery habit, opportunity solution tree, north-star metric, ...), every one evidence-free. The >=15 flagged threshold is DELIBERATELY STRICT and known-brittle: a working scorer that correctly flags only 12 of 15 borderline mirrors while crediting 3 defensible synonyms would fail this. Kept tight on purpose; revisit only via the iteration rules, never loosen silently.

assertions.must_have: enterprise B2B products into long, complex sales cycles (6 months or more)

G10.note: D outshines S on every section EXCEPT the required enterprise-6-month-cycle must-have (missing). S2 must-have double-weighting must drag D's composite below S, and D's gap report must surface the must-have as THE gap, phrased as a question.
